original_value: AbstractBackgroundPatients with rare diseases (RDs) are often diagnosed too late or not at all. Clinical decision support systems (CDSSs) could support the diagnosis in RDs. The MIRACUM (Medical Informatics in Research and Medicine) consortium, which is one of four funded consortia in the German Medical Informatics Initiative, will develop a CDSS for RDs based on distributed clinical data from ten university hospitals. This qualitative study aims to investigate (1) the relevant organizational conditions for the operation of a CDSS for RDs when diagnose patients (e.g. the diagnosis workflow), (2) which data is necessary for decision support, and (3) the appropriate user group for such a CDSS.MethodsInterviews were carried out with RDs experts. Participants were recruited from staff physicians at the Rare Disease Centers (RDCs) at the MIRACUM locations, which offer diagnosis and treatment of RDs.An interview guide was developed with a category-guided deductive approach. The interviews were recorded on an audio device and then transcribed into written form. We continued data collection until all interviews were completed. Afterwards, data analysis was performed using Mayring’s qualitative content analysis approach.ResultsA total of seven experts were included in the study. The results show that medical center guides and physicians from RDC B-centers (with a focus on different RDs) are involved in the diagnostic process. Furthermore, interdisciplinary case discussions between physicians are conducted.The experts explained that RDs exist which cannot be fully differentiated, but rather described only by their overall symptoms or findings: diagnosis is dependent on the disease or disease group. At the end of the diagnostic process, most centers prepare a summary of the patient case. Furthermore, the experts considered both physicians and experts from the B-centers to be potential users of a CDSS. The experts also have different experiences with CDSS for RDs.ConclusionsThis qualitative study is a first step towards establishing the requirements for the development of a CDSS for RDs. Further research is necessary to create solutions by also including the experts on RDs.

result.paraphrase: AbstractBackgroundRare diseases (RDs) are frequently diagnosed too late, or not diagnosed at all. Clinical decision support systems (CDSSs) may help improve RD diagnosis. The MIRACUM (Medical Informatics in Research and Medicine) consortium—one of four funded consortia within the German Medical Informatics Initiative—plans to develop an RD-focused CDSS using distributed clinical data from ten university hospitals. This qualitative study investigates: (1) the organizational requirements for operating an RD CDSS during patient diagnosis (for example, the diagnostic workflow), (2) which data are needed for decision support, and (3) the most suitable user group for such a system.MethodsWe conducted interviews with RD experts recruited from physicians working at the Rare Disease Centers (RDCs) at MIRACUM sites, which provide diagnosis and treatment for RDs.An interview guide was created using a category-guided deductive approach. Interviews were audio-recorded and transcribed. Data collection continued until all interviews had been completed. The data were then analyzed using Mayring’s qualitative content analysis method.ResultsSeven experts participated in the study. The findings indicate that medical center guides and physicians from RDC B-centers, each focused on different RDs, are involved in the diagnostic process. Interdisciplinary case discussions among physicians also take place.The experts noted that some RDs cannot be fully distinguished and can only be characterized by their overall symptoms or findings; in such cases, the diagnosis depends on the specific disease or disease group. By the end of the diagnostic process, most centers compile a summary of the patient case. The experts identified both physicians and experts from the B-centers as potential CDSS users. They also reported differing experiences with CDSSs for RDs.ConclusionsThis qualitative study is an initial step toward defining the requirements for developing a CDSS for RDs. Further research is needed to develop solutions that also incorporate RD experts.
